decisions.rationale: The user can reaffirm afternoon return departures. Considering near-afternoon options when true afternoon choices are limited or unattractive adds a reusable relaxation beyond the default, while a current-trip timing instruction is a valid override.
Choosing nonstop supports the policy. Calling it a preference merely repeats the prioritize-first default, while accepting a one-stop itinerary for a particular trip is a natural temporary override.

Including or favoring comparable Delta options is support. The soft, nonexclusive, comparability language is already encoded in the preference and default; choosing another carrier for current-trip constraints is an exception.

Selecting the cheapest acceptable itinerary supports the policy. Not overriding must-haves repeats the condition's acceptable-shortlist premise, while paying more for a current stated requirement is a valid exception.

Choosing a pool-and-fitness hotel, with hot tub as a bonus, is support. The core-versus-optional hierarchy already appears in the preference and default; waiving an amenity for the current stay is an exception.

Reaffirming the applicable rating floor is support. Binding the threshold to the rating metric under discussion, rather than hotel class or another rating system, is a reusable scope rule; a newly stated trip-specific threshold is an exception.

Selecting a beach-proximate hotel within walking distance supports the policy. Walking distance and coastal scope are already encoded, while a different current-trip location priority is a valid exception.
Choosing an afternoon departure is support. Excluding legs with an explicitly different requested time repeats the condition and scope and is a one-trip exception, not a durable boundary.

Choosing at most one short layover among connecting itineraries supports the policy. Restricting it to connecting itineraries repeats the condition and scope; a different stop requirement for one trip is an exception.

Including United among suitable carriers is support. Not uniquely ranking United is already encoded by the acceptable-carrier wording and inclusion default; excluding it for the current trip is an exception.

Requesting a window seat supports the policy. Deferring the attempt until check-in when selection is unavailable is an execution fallback, not an independent boundary; requesting another seat for one flight is an exception.
Choosing a queen bed for the shared room supports the policy. Per-room application is already encoded in the condition and scope, while requesting separate beds for the current room is an exception.

Choosing a room with both named amenities supports the policy. The warning against inferring unrelated travel preferences supplies no additional alternative behavior; relaxing an amenity for one stay is an exception.
Choosing a morning outbound flight supports the policy. Avoiding route, date, or leg inferences only restates its scoped time-of-day nature; a current-trip timing request is an exception.

Choosing an afternoon or evening return supports the policy. Describing that same interval as a flexible later-day window repeats the preference; another period requested for one trip is an exception.

Selecting or surfacing business class supports the policy. Its softness and coach fallback are already explicit in the preference, and the budget warning adds no concrete reusable alternative; declining business class for one trip is an exception.
Choosing nonstop supports the policy. Calling it nonabsolute repeats the prioritize-first default, while accepting a one-stop option for a trip with no suitable nonstop is a valid exception.

Requesting Marcus's window seat supports the policy. Trying later when seat selection is unavailable is execution fallback rather than boundary evidence; a different seat for a current itinerary is an exception.

Prioritizing a hotel with included breakfast supports the policy. Calling it soft repeats the stated preference and default, while making breakfast mandatory or waiving it for the current booking is a one-trip override.

Choosing a balcony room supports the policy. A first-floor room being acceptable without a balcony supplies a reusable counter-condition with different behavior, and accepting no balcony for a particular stay is a temporary override.
Choosing a morning departure supports the policy. The warning against inferring route, date, or leg requirements only restates its general scope; an explicit current-trip time is an exception.

Choosing the cheapest itinerary after requirements are met supports the policy. Protecting those requirements repeats the acceptable-option condition; selecting a costlier flight for a current must-have is an exception.

Including United among suitable options supports the policy. The prohibition on uniquely favoring it repeats the multi-carrier inclusion semantics, while excluding or bypassing United for the current trip is an exception.
Preferring business class supports the policy. Softness, coach fallback, and lack of a separate budget rule are already inherent or non-actionable; choosing coach for a current trip is an exception.

Applying the appropriate rating floor supports the policy. Keeping that floor tied to the rating metric under discussion is a reusable scope limit with concrete filtering consequences; a new trip-specific floor or metric is an exception.

Selecting a room with coffee maker and mini-fridge supports the policy. Not inferring unrelated amenities or trip attributes is only a non-inference warning; relaxing either amenity for one stay is an exception.

Prioritizing pool and fitness, then hot tub, supports the policy. The boundary repeats the already stated core-versus-additional amenity ranking; a current-stay waiver or stronger constraint is an exception.
Choosing an afternoon departure supports the policy. The explicit-other-time clause is already in scope and functions as a one-trip exception rather than a new reusable boundary.

Selecting no more than one short layover among connections supports the policy. Limiting application to connecting itineraries repeats the condition and scope; a different current stop requirement is an exception.

Selecting the cheapest acceptable flight supports the policy. Preserving explicit itinerary and amenity requirements repeats the acceptable-shortlist premise, while paying more for a current must-have is an exception.
Requesting a window seat supports the policy. Waiting until selection becomes available is fallback execution and not boundary evidence; a different seat request for one flight is an exception.

Choosing included breakfast supports the policy. The soft-preference statement repeats the default's prioritization behavior; making breakfast mandatory or dispensable for one booking is a temporary override.

Choosing a balcony room supports the policy. Accepting a first-floor room without one is a reusable counter-condition beyond mere prioritization, while waiving the balcony for a particular stay is an exception.

Choosing a nonstop itinerary supports the policy. Describing nonstop as nonabsolute repeats the preference/default, while confirming a one-stop option for a trip lacking suitable nonstop service is an exception.
Choosing an afternoon or evening return supports the policy. The flexible later-day wording restates that same range; selecting another period for the current trip is an exception.

Including and favoring comparable Delta options supports the policy. Softness and comparability are already encoded in the preference and condition; another carrier for current-trip constraints is an exception.
Requesting a window seat supports the policy. Trying again at check-in when booking-time selection is unavailable is execution fallback, while requesting another seat for one flight is an exception.

Choosing a queen bed for the couple's shared room supports the policy. Per-room application repeats the condition and scope; requesting twin, separate, or another arrangement for the current room is an exception.

Choosing a beach hotel within walking distance supports the policy. The walking-distance and coastal limitations already appear in the default and scope; another current-trip location priority is an exception.

Using the applicable rating floor supports the policy. Applying it only to the rating metric under discussion is a reusable scope limit that changes filtering behavior; a newly stated threshold or metric for one search is an exception.
